verifications.claim: NASA is currently targeting a mid-2027 launch for the Artemis III mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III Scheduled for 2027'; R3: 'Launch date Mid-2027 (planned)'; R4: 'Artemis III (mid-2027)'; R6: 'Artemis III to now mid-2027'; R10: 'Artemis III to Mid-2027'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state mid-2027 or 2027 as the current target for Artemis III launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III mission is designed to test in-orbit capabilities such as docking with commercial landers in low Earth orbit to prepare for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test in-orbit capabilities such as using the astronauts’ space suits in microgravity and rendezvousing with at least one of the spacecraft that NASA hopes to use as a lunar lander'; R2: 'test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'; R3: 'rendezvous in Earth orbit with one or both commercially developed Human Landing System (HLS) vehicles... test rendezvous and docking operations'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe Artemis III as an Earth orbit test mission involving docking/rendezvous with commercial landers (Starship HLS, Blue Moon) to validate systems for future landings.

verifications.claim: The timeline of the Artemis III mission depends on the success of the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The announcement... came after the agency’s Artemis II mission encountered problems, delaying its launch'; R3: 'Post-Artemis II landing[edit] The Artemis III mission is slated for possible improvements from the design of the Artemis II'; R4: Sequential missions with Artemis II in 2026 followed by III in 2027
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe sequential program structure and note II delays/problems impacting III planning, but do not explicitly state 'depends on the success'—implied by context.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is now set for 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'next launch window for Artemis II opens in early April'; R4: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026)'; R6: 'Artemis II is now slated for April 2026'; R10: 'Artemis II, is now planned for April 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently confirm Artemis II retargeted to April 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis III was originally meant for a 2026 lunar landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'In January 2024, NASA officially delayed Artemis III to no earlier than September 2026'; R6: 'Artemis III has been moved from 2025... to now mid-2027'; R10: 'Artemis III for mid-2027 instead of September 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm recent prior targeting of September 2026 for lunar landing before further delays and reconfiguration; aligns with 'originally' in program evolution context.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is now being reconfigured as a 2027 test mission to validate systems for future landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA will rejigger its planned Artemis III mission to test in-orbit capabilities... Instead the agency will rejigger... to test...'; R3: 'revised plan for Artemis III to perform tests... in Earth orbit... Artemis IV tentatively designated as the first crewed lunar landing'; R5: 'Artemis III mission, now in 2027, will be designed to test out systems... to prepare for an Artemis IV landing'
verifications.reasoning: Direct matches describe reconfiguration from landing to 2027 Earth-orbit test mission for system validation ahead of future landings.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III mission will use the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Rocket Space Launch System[5] Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'; R4: 'Each numbered mission centers on launching an SLS rocket carrying an Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state SLS as launch vehicle for Artemis III.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III mission will use the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Orion spacecraft will serve as the exploration vehicle that will carry and sustain the crew on Artemis missions'; R3: 'Spacecraft Orion CM-004 ESM-3'; R4: 'SLS rocket carrying an Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Orion as crew vehicle for Artemis III.

verifications.claim: Development challenges with the Human Landing System (HLS) and spacesuits have historically caused schedule slips.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'delays in the development of the Starship HLS... spacesuits would not be ready until April 2025 at the earliest, likely delaying the mission... NASA officially delayed Artemis III to no earlier than September 2026... December 2024, NASA officially delayed Artemis III to no earlier than 2027'; R7: 'challenges with spacesuits and lunar lander development... delays with the Human Landing System (HLS)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly attribute repeated schedule slips to HLS (Starship) and spacesuit development issues.
